content:
If I could go back in time and tell my younger self one thing, I already know what his reaction would be.

“Wait… we’re a lawyer?” 😳

And honestly, that thought gets me every time.

Because that kid had absolutely no idea where life was going to take him.

He didn’t know about the long nights, the doubts, the failures, the things that wouldn’t work out, or all the times I’d question whether I was doing enough.

He just knew what was in front of him.

And if I could show him where we are today, I think he’d be pretty amazed.

We spend so much time thinking about what’s still left to achieve that we forget there was a version of us who would have been incredibly proud just to see where we are now.

There are still two voices in my head.

One doubts almost everything.

What if I fail? 
What if I’m not ready? 
What if I can’t do it?

And the other one has a much simpler answer:

“You’ll figure it out.” 
Because somehow, I always have.

Then there are those moments when you walk into a room and realise you’re probably the youngest person there.

For a second, you wonder if you really belong.

Then you look around and think: 
“I’m the youngest in the room.
But I’m in the room.”

And maybe that’s enough.
It doesn’t mean you’re better than anyone.

It just means you might be a little further along than you thought you’d be.

Sometimes, you’re already living something that your younger self could only imagine.

And I think that’s worth pausing for.

Also, somewhere along the way, the younger version of me apparently wanted to be a photographer.

So the last two pictures are my very serious attempt at proving that dream is still alive.

But honestly, I like that part of me is still there. The part that notices a sunset, stops for a picture, and finds something worth capturing in an ordinary moment.

Maybe not every dream has to become a profession. Some can just remain a part of you.

So whenever I start worrying about how much is still left, I try to remember how much has already happened.

I don’t know exactly what comes next.
I don’t need to.

I’ll figure it out. I always do. Because I always have.

comment: A career rarely looks like a straight path from the inside. The bigger challenge is not reaching the room, but building the confidence and judgment to contribute once you’re there.
